Author: Juvvadi Sridevi
Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi

 Criminal Revision Case Nos.576 and 580 of 2007
Common Order :

Since the facts of the case and the issue involved are identical and since both these Criminal Revision Cases arise out of the same judgment, both these Criminal Revision Cases are taken up together and are being disposed of by this common order.

2. Crl.R.C.No.576 of 2007 is filed by the petitioner/A3 and Crl.R.C.No.580 of 2007 is filed by the petitioner/A2, challenging the judgment, dated 19.04.2007, passed in Criminal Appeal No.7 of 2007 by the V Additional Sessions Judge (III Fast Track Court), Nalgonda at Miryalguda,

whereby, the judgment, dated 08.01.2007, passed in C.C.No.275 of 2003 by the Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Huzurnagar, convicting the petitioners/A3 and A2 of the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) for violation of provisions under Section 7(i) and 2(ia) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ('the Act', for brevity) and sentencing them to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- each, in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for two months, was confirmed.

sentences.text: 3. I have heard the submissions of Sri Bharath Shah, learned counsel appearing for Sri S.Satyanarayana Murthy, learned counsel 2 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 for the petitioner in Crl.R.C.No.576 of 2007, Sri N.Harinath, learned counsel, appearing for Sri Masthan Naidu Cherukuri, learned counsel for the petitioner in Crl.R.C.No.580 of 2007 and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for the respondents in both these Criminal Revision Cases.

entities.text: Crl.R.C.No.580 of 2007 and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for the respondents in both these Criminal Revision Cases.

sentences.text: I have perused the record.
4. For convenience of discussion, the parties would be hereinafter referred as per their array before the trial Court.

5. The case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 17.12.2002 at about 12:40 hours, the complainant/Food Inspector, Nalgonda (PW.1) inspected Sri Lakshmi Traders, Nereducherla, along with his office attendant.
During the said visit, A1-Garine Saidaiah, proprietor of Sri Lakshmi Traders, was present and was transacting business.

PW.1 disclosed his identity to A1 in the presence of LW.2- Vijay Kumar, inspected the premises of Sri Lakshmi Traders and found 40 kilograms of Redgram Dal in an open gunny bag of 50 kilograms capacity, without label.
On enquiry by PW.1, A1 stated that the said Redgram Dal was kept for sale to public for human consumption and he purchased the same from M/s.

sentences.text: 1 (A2) under purchase bill No.6936, dated 05.12.2002

. On suspicion, PW.1 purchased 750 grams of Redgram Dal from the stock for Rs.18.75 ps under a cash receipt, served Form No.6 notice to A1 informing his 3 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 intention to send the said Redgram Dal to Public Analyst for analysis and

obtained acknowledgement, divided the purchased Redgram Dal into three equal parts of 250 grams each, placed the same into three separate empty dried and clean plastic jars, affixed label of local Health Authority and conducted panchanama,
which was attested by panch witness, PW.2.
On 18.12.2002, PW.1 sent one part of sealed sample to Public Analyst and the remaining two parts of sealed sample was deposited with local Health Authority, Nalgonda for safe custody.

PW.1 received Public Analyst Report under Ex.P18 with covering letter, dated 24.01.2003, who opined that the sample contains synthetic colour 'Tartrazine'
and is, therefore, adulterated.
On 31.01.2003, PW.1 addressed a letter bearing No.132/NLG/DII/5632/2002 to the supplier of said Redgram Dal (A2) asking him to furnish ownership/license particulars of the firm.
In response, A2 submitted the license particulars and stated that they have purchased the said stock of Redgram Dal from A3-M/s.

Vijaya Durga Dhal &
General Merchants, Macherla, Guntur District, vide bill No.3/9, dated 05.11.2002, and submitted the xerox copy of the same, which was received by PW.1 on 04.03.2003.
On 04.03.2003, PW.1 sent a notice in Form-VI under Section 14A of the Act along with a letter to A3, asking him to furnish their license/ownership particulars by registered post.

However, the said letter returned undelivered by the postal authorities with an endorsement 'not in 4 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 &
580 of 2007 mill'.

On 21.03.2003, PW.1 addressed a letter to the Assistant Food Controller,
Zone-III, Headquarters Guntur, with a request to furnish the license particulars of the A3 Firm, but however, there was no response.
Thereafter, on 01.04.2003, PW.1 made further efforts and addressed a letter along with Form-VI notice to A3 firm, which was also returned undelivered.

Thereafter, on 17.06.2003, PW.1 submitted a detailed report to the State Food (Health) Authority through Gazetted Food Inspector & Local (Health) Authority, Nalgonda District, seeking necessary orders.

On 15.07.2003, PW.1 addressed a letter to the Assistant Commercial Tax Officer, Macherla,
Guntur District, requesting to furnish license particulars of A3 Firm.

In response, the Food Inspector, Division-III, Guntur District, has furnished license and ownership particulars of A3, vide letter No.301/ZIII/2003, dated 23.07.2003, along with letter submitted by the A3.
The Assistant Commercial Tax Officer, Macherla, Guntur District, also furnished the license/ownership particulars of A3 vide Lr.No.NRP/D-7/1/2729, dated 25.07.2003.
PW.1 submitted the said particulars to the Director & Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad on 14.08.2003.

The State Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad has accorded written consent under Section 20(1) of the Act for launching the prosecution against A1 to A3, vide order, dated 20.09.2003, for selling adulterated Redgram Dal for human consumption.

As there was some mistake in 5 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 mentioning the name of A3, the Gazetted Food Inspector & Local (Health) Authority, Nalgonda District, vide letter, dated 08.10.2003, requested the State Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad, to issue necessary corrigendum to the written consent orders, dated 20.09.2003.
Accordingly, the State Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, has issued corrigendum, dated 18.11.2003.
Pursuant to the permission to launch prosecution, PW.1 filed the subject complaint before the trial Court on 18.12.2003 and issued notice under Section 13(2) of the Act to A1 to A3 on 24.12.2003.

sentences.text:
The learned Magistrate took cognizance against A1 to A3 on 20.12.2003, for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Act for violation of provisions of Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(i)
of the Act.
To prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined P.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.52.

On behalf of the accused, no evidence, either oral or documentary, has been adduced.
7.

The trial Court, after analysing the entire evidence on record, while acquitting A1 of the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Act for violation of provisions of Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(i)
of the Act, found A2 and A3 guilty of the said offence and accordingly, convicted and sentenced them as stated supra.
Aggrieved thereby, A2 and A3 preferred the subject Criminal Appeal 6 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 No.07 of 2007 before the Court below.
The Court below, after re- appreciating the entire material available on record, dismissed the appeal, by confirming the judgment passed by the trial Court.
Aggrieved by the same, A2 and A3 preferred both these Criminal Revision Cases.
8. The learned counsel for the petitioners/A2 and A3 would submit that both the Courts below erred in properly appreciating the evidence on record.
PW.2, a panch witness, did not support the case of prosecution and his evidence is not corroborated with the evidence of PW.1.
Taking this Court through the chronology of events, learned counsel for the petitioners/A2 and A3 submitted that the sample of the alleged adulterated Redgram Dal was lifted on 17.12.2002.
Permission to launch prosecution against the accused was sanctioned on 20.09.2003.
PW.1 filed the subject complaint before the Court below on 18.12.2003 and a notice under Section 13(2) of the Act was issued to the petitioners/A2 and A3 on 24.12.2003.

Hence, there was inordinate delay in launching prosecution against the petitioners/A2 and A3, which deprived their valuable right under section 13(2) of the Act to seek permission to send the sample to the Central Food Laboratory for second analysis.

Further,
as per Section 11(4) of the Act, an article of food seized under Section 10(4) and any adulterant seized under Section 10(6) of the Act shall be produced before the Magistrate as soon as possible,
not later than 7 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 seven days after the receipt of report of Public Analyst, which is patently absent in the instant case.
Further, the very collection of sample was not in accordance with the relevant Rules and drawing of sample itself was wrong.

The action against the petitioners/A2 and A3 stands vitiated on account of inordinate and deliberate delay in launching prosecution against them, thereby depriving them of the valuable rights conferred under the Act.
Both the Courts below erroneously convicted the petitioners/A2 and A3 of the offence alleged against them.

It is a fit case to extend benefit of doubt to the petitioners/A2 and A3 and acquit them of the offence alleged against them and ultimately prayed to allow the Criminal Revision Cases as prayed for.
9.

On the other hand, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor supported the judgment impugned in these Criminal Revision Cases and contended that there are no circumstances to interfere with the impugned judgment.

Taking this Court through the contents of the complaint lodged by PW.1 and the evidence of PWs.1 and 2, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submitted that merely because of the delay, no prejudice has been caused to the petitioners/A2 and A3.
The delay occurred only in the process of securing the sanction from the Government.
There are no procedural irregularities in launching prosecution against the petitioners/A2 and A3.

The evidence placed 8 Justice Juvvadi T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P., on 28 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156749863/
3 Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 on record clinchingly proves the guilt of the petitioners/A2 and A3 beyond all reasonable doubt for the offences alleged against them.

entities.text: Juvvadi T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the trial Court was justified in convicting and sentencing the petitioners/A2 and A3, which was rightly confirmed by the Court below.
Both these Criminal Revision Cases are devoid of merit and are liable to be dismissed and ultimately prayed to dismiss the Criminal Revision Cases.

10. In view of the above submissions, the point that arises for determination in these two Criminal Revision Cases is as follows:
"Whether the impugned judgment, dated 19.04.2007, passed in Criminal Appeal No.7 of 2007 by the V Additional Sessions Judge (III Fast Track Court), Nalgonda at Miryalguda, convicting and sentencing the petitioners/A2 and A3 of the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) for violation of provisions under Section 7(i) and 2(ia) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is legally sustainable?"

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge (III Fast Track Court), Nalgonda at Miryalguda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: POINT:-
11. The petitioners/A2 and A3 were convicted for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) for violation of provisions under Section 7(i) and 2(ia) of the Act.

A1 in this case was acquitted of the said offence on the ground that the evidence collected by the prosecution against him was not sufficient for reaching to an undoubted conclusion that he was responsible for the alleged offence and that he is entitled for 9 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 protection under Section 19(2)
of the Act.

While the petitioners/A2 and A3 would contend that due to deliberate and inordinate delay in launching prosecution against them, they have lost their valuable right of sending the second sample to the Analyst under Section 13(2) of the Act and that there was clear violation of the mandatory stipulation contained in Section 11(4) of the Act regarding production of the remaining sample before the Court, the prosecution contends that merely because there was delay in filing the complaint, no prejudice has been caused to the petitioners/A2 and A3 and the same would not, in any event, vitiate the whole prosecution case.

12. The relevant events and dates, which are crucial for determining the present lis, are as under:
 Date of lifting the samples 17.12.2002  Date of sending the samples to  18.12.2002  the Analyst  Date on which the Public Analyst  22.01.2003  sent his report  Date of filing of the complaint 18.12.2003  Date of issuance of notice under  24.12.2003  Section 13(2) of the Act T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P., on 28 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156749863/
4 13.

entities.text: T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Here, it is apt to extract Section 11 (4) of the Act, which reads as follows:
11. Procedure to be followed by food inspectors -- (1) xxxx (2) xxxx (3) xxxx 10 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 (4) An article of food seized under sub-section (4) of section 10, unless destroyed under subsection (4A) of that section, and any adulterant seized under sub-section (6) of that section shall be produced before a magistrate as soon as possible and in any case not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the public analyst

Provided that if an application is made to the magistrate in this behalf by the person from whom any article of food has been seized, the magistrate shall by order in writing direct the food inspector to produce such article before him within such time as may be specified in the order.
(5) xxxx (6) xxxx 14.

A plain reading of the above extracted sub-section (4) of Section 11 of the Act makes it clear that an article of food seized under Sub-section 4 of Section 10 and any adulterant seized under Sub-section (6) of Section 10 shall be produced before a Magistrate as soon as possible, and in any case, not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the Public Analyst.
In the instant case, the seized sample, admittedly, was not produced before the Court within seven days as required under Sub-section 4 of Section 11 of the Act.
Thus, there is clear violation of the mandatory stipulation contained under Section 11(4) of the Act regarding production of the sample before the Court.

The inordinate delay of about one year in producing the sample before the Court from the date of lifting the sample and also from the date of receipt of the Public Analyst Report would certainly cause prejudice to the petitioners/A2 and A3, which is detrimental to their defence.
There is absolutely no explanation offered by the prosecution for the abnormal delay in production of 11 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 the sample before the Court.

The Court below, while discussing the said aspect, held that whatever delay occurred in this case is only in the process of securing the sanctioning from the Government to launch prosecution and that there is no delay on the part of the Food Inspector or the local (Health) Authority, Nalgonda.

The said observation, in my view, is erroneous, inasmuch as no person can be deprived of his valuable right conferred upon him/her under a statute because of administrative delay in securing sanction of prosecution against a person.

15. Further, Section 13(2) of the Act reads as follows:
On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons,
as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P., on 28 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156749863/
5

entities.text: T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.

16. In the instant case, the Public Analyst Report was obtained on 22.01.2003 and the complaint was filed only on 18.12.2003, i.e., after about eleven months, and the opportunity, as provided under Section 13(2) of the Act, was denied to the petitioners/A2 and A3.

There is no explanation for lodging the subject complaint belatedly after about eleven months, when the Public Analyst Report was very 12 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 much available with the complainant as on 22.01.2003.
Though the Public Analyst submitted his report on 22.01.2003, the Prosecution could not file the complaint till 18.12.2003.
After filing of complaint, notice under Section 13(2) of the Act, was issued to the petitioners/A2 and A3 on 24.12.2003, which is evident from the material placed on record.
Thus, there was delay of about 11 months in affording opportunity to the petitioners/A2 and A3 for getting the sample analyzed through the Central Food Laboratory.
Therefore it can unhesitatingly be held that the petitioners/A2 and A3 have lost their valuable opportunity of getting the sample analyzed through Central Food Laboratory.

The inordinate delay on the part of the prosecution is not attributable to the petitioners/A2 and A3 and,
therefore, the consequences thereof cannot work adversely to the interest of the petitioners/A2 and A3.
As the valuable right of the petitioners/A2 and A3 for reanalysis provided under the Act appears to have been violated, their prosecution, if allowed to continue, would be a lame prosecution.
No convincing reason is given as to why the complaint could not be lodged for such a long period.

17. A meticulous examination of the entire material placed on record reveals that the statutory rights under Sections 11(4) and 13(2) of the Act have been virtually denied to the petitioners/A2 and A3,
owing the fault on the part of the prosecution.
The said statutory 13 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 rights are valuable and indefeasible.
They cannot be taken away in any circumstance.
By launching the prosecution after an unexplained delay of about one year from the date of lifting of the sample, the rights of the petitioners/A2 and A3 have been smothered in this case.

Therefore, the prosecution launched against the petitioners/A2 and A3 cannot be sustained in the eye of law, it being violative of indefeasible rights of the petitioners/A2 and A3 under Sections 11(4) and 13(2) of the Act.

By deprivation of these rights, the petitioners/A2 and A3 have been denied an opportunity to prove their defence and hence, the prosecution was only one sided, which is against the well settled principles of Criminal Jurisprudence.
Therefore, to secure the ends of justice, the prosecution of the petitioners/A2 and A3 of the offences alleged against them is liable to be set aside.
18. For these reasons, both these Criminal Revision Cases are allowed.

The conviction and sentence recorded against the petitioners/A2 and A3 under Section 16(1)(a)(1) for violation of Provisions under Section 7(1) and 2(ia) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, vide judgment, dated 08.01.2007, passed in C.C.No.275 of 2003 by the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Huzurnagar,
and confirmed by the Court below vide judgment dated 19.04.2007, passed in Criminal Appeal No.7 of 2007 by the V 14 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 Additional Sessions Judge (III Fast Track Court), Nalgonda at Miryalguda, are hereby set aside.

The bail bonds of the petitioners/A2 and A3 shall stand cancelled and the fine amount, if any, paid by them shall be T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P., on 28 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156749863/
6 refunded to them.
